notes: Terraqueous Globe - Natural Earth II, stated in the map's own legend ('Compromise pseudocylindrical projection Natural Earth II') and confirmed by measurement. The NE-II envelope was fitted in S2 (2026-07-23) by tracing the oval's drawn boundary curve across 2001 rows and least-squares fitting the envelope to it, giving centre (1999.55, 1129.29), scale sx=702.2114 sy=702.6857, inlier RMS 0.363 px with every traced row inside 10 px. Two independent checks pass - sx/sy = 0.99933 (isotropic, i.e. drawn to true NE-II proportions, which a wrong polynomial could not produce alongside a sub-pixel envelope fit), and the fitted graticule lands within ~2 px of the map's own printed degree labels (170W at x=234, measured 236; equator y=1129, measured 1130; 20S y=1378, measured 1377). RE-EMITTED for the Miller canvas (2026-08-04): the S2 fit above is a property of the ARTWORK, not of the canvas, so it was recovered unchanged from the previous record (0.0019 px rms) and re-evaluated at graticule crossings inside the new band. The two old polar picks could not be migrated - they sat at lat +-79.453125, which under Miller is y = -258.6 and +4463.2, off the canvas - so the edge picks are now the band's own limits, 74.9052N and 57.4084S. reproject.py recovers the same four constants from this table to 0.002 px. Crop is the oval interior, inset ~4 px from the drawn boundary rule so the black envelope line is never sampled; the generator clamps into the crop rather than masking, because the canvas seam at lon +-180 lands exactly on that rule. The polar insets (from y=2148) and the title/legend block sit outside it. Highest coastline precedence: this is the only whole-world source registered to sub-pixel accuracy, so it - not the regional relief - defines the shoreline. MIGRATED to the Miller canvas frame (migrate_frame_coords.py, 2026-08-04).
